Girders per superstructure

specs.label: Mapped geometry
specs.value: two one way decks, about 27 m each

differences: Paper reports two first natural frequencies (4.33 Hz simulated, 5.32 Hz measured first longitudinal mode); not in record, just a caveat if used.

Record history says 'additional upstream and downstream gauges for axle detection'; paper says one upstream and one downstream gauge per instrumented lane in a NOR system (no axle detectors on the pavement). Wording 'axle detection' is an interpretation.

Traffic layout: González et al. write "a two-lane simply supported structure with traffic in opposite directions", while the IM-SAFE case study describes two independent superstructures, one for each travel direction, and OpenStreetMap maps two one way decks.
Span: 25 m in the IM-SAFE case study against 24.8 m between supports and 26 m in total in O'Brien et al.
vransko.open: Which of the two decks carried the SiWIM system. Year of construction (González et al. call it a 10 year old bridge at the time of the 2006 measurements).

he_zlatolicje.summary: HE Zlatoličje, diversion (canal) hydropower plant on the Drava system, fed from the Melje weir in Maribor; powerhouse near Zlatoličje, Municipality of Starše; owner Dravske elektrarne Maribor (DEM, HSE Group).

specs.label: Dam type
specs.value: no dam at the powerhouse; intake weir is Jez Melje (see jez_melje)

specs.label: Refurbishment scope
specs.value: electromechanical upgrade, dam refurbishment, mini HPP on ecological flow, downstream landscaping

differences: Installed capacity disagrees across sources: 136 MW (record 'typ', en.wikipedia Zlatoličje article), 126 MW (power-technology; record facts), 114 MW (en.wikipedia list of power stations, probably pre-refurbishment), max 133.2 MW (UM thesis 2009). Record 'typ' (136 MW) and 'facts' (126 MW) contradict each other.
Commissioning: power-technology gives commercial operation 1968; record gives first unit trial 19 Oct 1968 and official opening 26 Apr 1969 (compatible). Wikipedia: 'opened in 1969'.
Refurbishment dates: record 2006-2013; power-technology 2007-2012; Hydropower & Dams 2008 article describes it as ongoing.
'crosses: Drava' is misleading: the powerhouse is on the derivation canal (Hidroinštitut paper calls Melje/Zlatoličje a derivation-type plant).
power-technology lists 'gross head 33 m, net head 5.9 m', which looks internally inconsistent; not used.
The same source gives two units of 79 MW each, which adds up to 158 MW, not 126 MW.
Installed capacity: 136 MW (wiki.riteme.site) against 126 MW Zlatoličje hydro project (balkangreenenergynews.com)
Installed capacity: 136 MW (wiki.riteme.site) against 114 (list row 'HPP Zlatoličje | Drava | Zlatoličje | Run-of-river | 114 | 1969-') (en.wikipedia.org)

specs.label: Us4f partners
specs.value: City of Maribor, ZAG, IPI, Aktiviraj se, WCYCLE, Deltaplan, Snaga

differences: Record years 2017-2022: CINDERELA ran 1 Jun 2018 - 30 Nov 2022 (CORDIS); Urban Soil 4 Food was scheduled to end Nov 2020 (EC Regio).
Record says 'more than 7,000 m2' of urban gardens planned; EC Regio says the urban gardens are on a 12,400 m2 plot (66 plots in the first garden).

CORDIS does not say the CINDERELA Slovenian demos were in Maribor; it lists Maribor partners Nigrad (Zagrebška cesta 30) and RRA Podravje. Location of CINDERELA pilots in Maribor rests on cinderela.eu, which I could not fetch.
maribor_pilots.open: the pilot sites are not placed by any source.

kamnik_bridges.summary: Unidentified bridges, ZAG 2015 damage assessment for the Municipality of Kamnik.
kamnik_bridges.open: the record names no single bridge, so it stays a municipal area.

sij_acroni_pavers.summary: Cement-free alkali-activated (geopolymer) pavers with 62% SIJ Acroni steel slag (78% secondary raw materials) laid at a bicycle parking area in front of / in the courtyard of the SIJ Acroni plant, Jesenice; GEORIS (EIT RawMaterials, lead Enalos); demo event 24 Apr 2024 with KU Leuven mobile unit.

specs.label: Composition
specs.value: 62% SIJ Acroni slag, 78% industrial secondary raw materials, cement-free

specs.label: Location detail
specs.value: bicycle parking in front of the SIJ Acroni plant

specs.label: Pavers produced
specs.value: more than 20 m2 manufactured and cured in a mobile unit

specs.label: Project
specs.value: GEORIS, 11 partners, lead Enalos, EIT RawMaterials; SI partners ZAG, SIJ Acroni, GeoZS, Gorenjska gradbena družba

differences: Record says pavers at 'SIJ Acroni headquarters'; SIJ says bicycle parking in front of the steel plant, the UM chapter says SIJ Acroni courtyard.
Record 'built: 2024': pavers already laid before the 24 Apr 2024 event; laying date not given.

golo_rebro.summary: Golo Rebro tunnel, A1 Štajerska motorway, Žiče to Dramlje, twin tube (1976 and 1996), at Blato, Žiče, Slovenske Konjice

specs.label: Opened
specs.value: first tube July 1976; second tube October 1996

differences: History text says 'Structurae gives 788 m for the 1996 tube' (golorebrotunnel-1996 page, unreadable this pass). The readable Structurae page gives eastern 750 / western 786 m, completion 1976. Lotsberg gives 788 m for the 1976 tube (21.07.1976) and 757 m for the 1996 tube (25.10.1996). So 788 m is attributed to the 1976 tube by Lotsberg; which tube is 788 m is unresolved.
length_m 788 in the record conflicts with Structurae's 786/750 m; OSM geometry 764 / 731 m.
Tube lengths: 786 m left and 786 m right (URSZR Celje) (gov.si) against 750 east / 786 west (Structurae), 788 / 757 (Lotsberg, en.wikipedia A1) (structurae.net)

ratece_cable.summary: Not confirmed which installation. The client Smuk is named as lift operator and concession holder of the Macesnovc ski area in Rateče, which has a two seat chairlift and two short tows.

specs.label: Candidate lift: macesnovec
specs.value: 2-CLF Doppelmayr, built 2004, commissioned 14 Jan 2006, 1300 m, 330 m rise, 870-1200 m, 1100 p/h, Icolan seats

specs.label: Lifts 2006
specs.value: Lom 1, 2-SED, 1975, 860/1172 m, 1010 m, 1200 p/h; operator Športni center Rateče Planica, Teslova 3, Ljubljana

specs.label: Concession for Macesnovc
specs.value: Smuk, Ljubljana, as reported on 12 March 2016

differences: Same coordinate as planica_z (Rateče settlement centre).
Facts list has duplicate 'Years' and 'Year' = 2012.

origin and year of the Macesnovc chairlift: Doppelmayr, year of construction 2004, commissioned 14 Jan 2006 (lift-world) (lift-world.info) against first installed in Austria, moved to Slovenia in 2005 (Gorenjski glas) (arhiv.gorenjskiglas.si)
vertical rise: 330 m, 870 to 1200 m (lift-world) (lift-world.info) against 316 m, 866 to 1,182 m (skiresort.com, sl. Wikipedia text via wikiwand) (skiresort.com)
slope length: 1,900 metres track (English Wikipedia, Rateče) (en.wikipedia.org) against 1500 m dolga proga (Slovenian Wikipedia text via wikiwand) (wikiwand.com)

operator address: Smuk, Teslova ulica 30, Ljubljana (skiresort.com) (skiresort.com) against Športni center Rateče Planica, Teslova 3, Ljubljana, lift 'Lom 1' 2-SED 1975 (2006 official list) (uradni-list.si)
ratece_cable.open: No ZAG document names the lift. Macesnovc was reported closed for eight years before February 2016, which covers the 2012 inspection year.
